[THOUGHT] A unilateral resting tremor that is increased by stress together with mild rigidity on exam is most consistent with parkinsonism. Essential tremor and cerebellar causes usually produce postural/action or intention tremors rather than an isolated resting tremor. Drug-induced parkinsonism is typically more symmetric and would require a medication history (not provided) to favor it. Although bradykinesia — a cardinal sign for Parkinson disease — was not clearly present, early idiopathic Parkinson disease can present primarily with a unilateral resting tremor and only subtle or initially absent bradykinesia. Given the age (70), progressive unilateral resting tremor, and exam findings of rigidity, the single most likely diagnosis is idiopathic Parkinson disease.

[DIAGNOSIS] Parkinson disease (idiopathic Parkinsonism)
